title: Seagrass loss in the Indian River Lagoon did not make Florida manatee winter death totals more sensitive to cold in 1987-2026, but in starvation winters more deaths occurred in cold months
abstract: Question: nutrient pollution removed most seagrass in Florida's Indian River Lagoon (IRL) in 2011 and 2019-2021, and starving manatees died in large numbers from December 2020. Did this habitat loss make IRL manatee winter deaths more sensitive to cold, relative to other Florida regions? Data: FWC-FWRI carcass records (1974-2023) and preliminary monthly county tables (2024-2026); NOAA GHCN-daily chilling degree-days below 15 C; 7 regions, 40 winters (1987-2026), 7,137 deaths that were not human-related and not perinatal. Methods: a plan written before the outcome models; Poisson models with region x era levels and IRL x era cold slopes; season bootstrap. Results: (1) Season totals (planned primary test): the change of the extra IRL cold slope from 1987-2011 to 2021-2026 was -0.75 log deaths per 100 C-days (95% CI -2.9 to +9.8). The 2021 and 2022 winters had 348 and 370 IRL deaths at ordinary cold, and the cold 2025/26 winter had only 34. The starvation deaths were a level shift, not an increase per unit of cold. (2) A post hoc within-winter model with a fixed effect for each region-season found that, in the starvation era, more IRL deaths occurred in and after cold months: slope change +1.5 (cluster CI +0.1 to +2.9; bootstrap -0.1 to +2.8), +2.3 (bootstrap +0.7 to +3.3) with Atlantic controls. Cold in the next two months (placebo) and watercraft deaths (negative control) gave no positive change, and no single winter removed the sign. (3) Since 2020, 56-72% of these carcasses in all regions were not necropsied, so the 'cold stress' label fell from 44% to 3% of IRL deaths; labelled cold deaths are not a valid series after 2020. Conclusion: seagrass loss did not make winter death totals depend more on winter cold, but cold appears to time the deaths of starved manatees. Limitations: 6 starvation-era winters; the timing result is post hoc and two of three bootstrap intervals include zero; air temperature, not refuge water temperature; no population denominator; carcass detection may also follow cold.
